'''Ime Sunday Udoka''' {{Audio|LL-Q33578 (ibo)-Vivian Amalachukwu-Ime Sunday Udoka.wav|Listen|help=no}} ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|iː|m|eɪ|_|uː|ˈ|d|oʊ|k|ə}} {{respell|EE|may|_|ooh|DOH|kə}};<ref name=":1" /> born August 9, 1977) is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is the head coach for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Born in the United States, he represented the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team|Nigeria national team]] during his playing career. After retiring as a player, Udoka served as an assistant coach with the [[San Antonio Spurs]], [[Philadelphia 76ers]], and [[Brooklyn Nets]] before becoming the head coach of the [[Boston Celtics]], whom he led to the [[2022 NBA Finals]]. In April 2023, Udoka was hired by the Rockets.

==Early life==
Ime Udoka was born to Vitalis and Agnes Udoka on August 9, 1977, in [[Portland, Oregon]]. Vitalis moved to the United States from Nigeria in 1970 while Agnes was an American from Illinois. Udoka attended [[Jefferson High School (Portland, Oregon)|Jefferson High School]] in Portland.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Source: Celtics hire former Trail Blazer Ime Udoka as new coach
|url=https://www.kgw.com/article/sports/celtics-hire-portland-native-ime-udoka-new-coach/283-5c7c94d5-2b4a-4d80-9a43-35c6a570dccc|access-date=2021-08-31|website=kgw8.com|date=June 23, 2021 }}</ref>

==College career==
Udoka played for [[Utah State University Eastern|College of Eastern Utah]] and the [[San Francisco Dons men's basketball|University of San Francisco]] before transferring to [[Portland State University]], where he starred for the [[Portland State Vikings|Vikings]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Celtics hire Ime Udoka as next coach|url=https://www.nba.com/news/celtics-hire-ime-udoka-as-next-coach|access-date=2021-08-31|website=www.nba.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Fargo-Moorhead Beez (2000–2001)===

After going undrafted in the [[2000 NBA draft]], Udoka began his professional basketball career in the minor leagues, including a stint with the [[Fargo-Moorhead Beez]] of the International Basketball Association during the 2000–01 season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Shelburne |first=Ramona |title=How Ime Udoka’s long basketball journey shaped his coaching career |url=https://www.espn.com/ |work=ESPN |date=2022 |access-date=23 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ime Udoka Minor League Basketball Statistics |url=https://www.statscrew.com/minorbasketball/stats/p-udokaime001 |website=StatsCrew}}</ref>

===Independiente (2001)===
Udoka played with [[Club Sportivo Independiente|Independiente]] in 2001.{{Citation needed|date=April 2025}}

===North Charleston Lowgators (2002–2003)===
Udoka played with the [[North Charleston Lowgators]] from 2002 to 2003.{{Citation needed|date=April 2025}}

===Adirondack Wildcats (2003)===
Udoka played for the [[Adirondack Wildcats]] of the [[United States Basketball League]] in 2003, where he averaged 19.4 points and 9.2 rebounds in 15 games.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ime Udoka Signs with Lakers |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/ime-udoka-signs-with-lakers/n-2340284 |website=OurSports Central}}</ref>

===Charleston Lowgators (2003–2004)===
Udoka played in the [[NBA Development League|NBDL]] with the [[Charleston Lowgators]], who drafted him with 39th overall pick in the 2002 [[NBA Development League|NBDL]] Draft.<ref>{{cite web |title=2002-03 NBDL Draft Board |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/nbdl/draft_board.html |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070815082340/http://www.nba.com/dleague/nbdl/draft_board.html |archive-date=August 15, 2007 |date=October 31, 2002}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2004)===
On January 14, 2004, Udoka signed a 10-day contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2004-01-14 |title=Lakers sign Udoka to 10-day contract |url=https://www.espn.com/wnba/news/story?id=1708766 |access-date=January 31, 2004 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Fort Worth Flyers (2005–2006)===
After a stint in Europe, which included a brief summer contract with [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]], Lithuanian champions and Euroleague participants, Udoka returned to the United States and was once again drafted in NBDL. This time, he was drafted third overall by the [[Fort Worth Flyers]] in the 2005 NBDL Draft.<ref>{{cite web |title=2005 NBA D-League Draft Board |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/draft_board_05.html |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101202102451/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/draft_board_05.html |archive-date=December 2, 2010 |date=November 3, 2005}}</ref> Udoka averaged 17.1 points and 6.2 rebounds per game with the Flyers.<ref name="mysanantonio" />

===New York Knicks (2006)===
On April 6, 2006, Udoka signed with the [[New York Knicks]]. He appeared in eight games, averaging 2.8 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 0.8 assists in 14.3 minutes.<ref name=":2" /> Udoka was waived on September 11.

===Portland Trail Blazers (2006–2007)===
Udoka was the last player invited to his hometown [[Portland Trail Blazers]]' training camp before the 2006–07 season, getting the invitation only after [[Aaron Miles (basketball)|Aaron Miles]] failed a [[Physical examination|physical]]. Despite the death of his father during the preseason,<ref name="goviks">{{cite web |title=Nigeria - Former Viking Ime Udoka makes his way |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/news/Nigeria-Former-Viking-Ime-Udoka-makes-his-way |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327130408/http://www.fiba.basketball/news/Nigeria-Former-Viking-Ime-Udoka-makes-his-way |archive-date=March 27, 2020 |date=February 16, 2007}}</ref> Udoka impressed the coaching staff with his defensive skills and made the team.{{citation needed|date=March 2020}}

Udoka was the last player invited to his hometown [[Portland Trail Blazers]]' training camp before the 2006–07 season after an opening emerged when [[Aaron Miles (basketball)|Aaron Miles]] failed his [[physical examination|physical]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Portland Invites Aaron Miles To Training Camp |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/179741/Portland-Invites-Aaron-Miles-To-Training-Camp |website=RealGM |date=27 September 2006}}</ref> He impressed the coaching staff with his defensive ability and earned a place on the regular-season roster.<ref>{{cite web |last=Dewald |first=Steven |title=McMillan Knew Former Trail Blazers Forward Ime Udoka was Destined for Coaching |url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2021/6/30/22557548/ime-udoka-nate-mcmillan-boston-celtics-trail-blazers-nba |website=Blazer's Edge |date=30 June 2021}}</ref>

After having played in only 12 NBA games in his career, Udoka started all 75 games he played in during the 2006–07 season. Udoka averaged 8.4 points, 3.7 rebounds, 1.5 assists, and 0.9 steals in 28.6 minutes per game.<ref name=":2" />

===San Antonio Spurs (2007–2009)===
In 2007, Udoka signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref name="mysanantonio">{{cite web |last1=Monroe |first1=Mike |title=Spurs: Udoka agrees to contract |url=http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/stories/MYSA081407.Spurs.Udoka.en.35bc859.html |website=mysanantonio.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070825181735/http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/stories/MYSA081407.Spurs.Udoka.en.35bc859.html |archive-date=August 25, 2007 |date=August 13, 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Spurs add Blazers' sniper Udoka |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2977652 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327130812/https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2977652 |archive-date=March 27, 2020 |date=August 16, 2007}}</ref> He played in 73 games, averaging 5.8 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 0.9 assists in 18 minutes per game.<ref name=":2" />

In his second season with the Spurs, Udoka played in 67 games and started in three, averaging 4.3 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 0.8 assists in 15.4 minutes per game.<ref name=":2">{{cite web |title=Ime Udoka Career Stats Page |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ime_udoka/career_stats.html |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120831191830/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ime_udoka/career_stats.html |archive-date=August 31, 2012}}</ref>

After the 2009 season, Udoka became a free agent and eventually re-signed with the Trail Blazers on September 25, 2009.<ref>{{cite web |title=Trail Blazers Sign Ime Udoka |url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail_blazers_sign_ime_udoka_2009_09_25.html |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090928072022/http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail_blazers_sign_ime_udoka_2009_09_25.html |archive-date=September 28, 2009 |date=September 25, 2009}}</ref> However, he was waived on October 22.<ref>{{cite web |title=Udoka, Collins waived by Blazers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/4586607 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327125849/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/4586607 |archive-date=March 27, 2020 |date=October 22, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Quick |first1=Jason |title=Ime Udoka: 'I thought these times were behind me ...' |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/behindblazersbeat/2009/10/ime_udoka_i_thought_these_time.html |website=oregonlive.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327123056/https://www.oregonlive.com/behindblazersbeat/2009/10/ime_udoka_i_thought_these_time.html |archive-date=March 27, 2020 |date=October 22, 2009}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2009–2010)===
On November 4, 2009, Udoka signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Kings sign Ime Udoka |url=https://www.foxsports.com/nba/story/kings-sign-ime-udoka-110409 |website=FOX Sports |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327111850/https://www.foxsports.com/nba/story/kings-sign-ime-udoka-110409 |archive-date=March 27, 2020 |date=November 4, 2009}}</ref> He played in 69 games and started in two, averaging 3.6 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 0.8 assists in 13.7 minutes per game.<ref name=":2" />

===Return to San Antonio (2010–2011)===
[[File:Ime Udoka 2.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Udoka in 2010]]
On November 24, 2010, Udoka re-signed with the Spurs.<ref>{{cite web |title=Spurs Sign Ime Udoka |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs_sign_ime_udoka_101124.html |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101127150436/https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs_sign_ime_udoka_101124.html |archive-date=November 27, 2010 |date=November 24, 2010}}</ref> However, he was waived on January 5, 2011, after playing in 20 games and averaging only 0.7 points, 0.9 rebounds, and 0.7 assists in 6.5 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Spurs Waive Ime Udoka |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs_waive_ime_udoka_110105.html |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110108195813/https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs_waive_ime_udoka_110105.html |archive-date=January 8, 2011 |date=January 5, 2011}}</ref>

===New Jersey Nets (2011)===
On December 15, 2011, Udoka signed with the [[New Jersey Nets]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NETS Sign Ime Udoka |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Udoka_Signing_Release_111215.html |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120123031546/http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Udoka_Signing_Release_111215.html |archive-date=January 23, 2012 |date=December 15, 2011}}</ref> However, he was waived on eight days later and did not appear in any games.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Castillo |first1=Jorge |title=Nets finalize roster by waiving Ime Udoka, keeping Linwood native Dennis Horner |url=https://www.nj.com/nets/2011/12/nets_finalize_roster_by_waivin.html |website=NJ.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327125036/https://www.nj.com/nets/2011/12/nets_finalize_roster_by_waivin.html |archive-date=March 27, 2020 |date=December 24, 2011}}</ref>

===UCAM Murcia (2012)===
On January 5, 2012, Udoka signed with [[UCAM Murcia CB|UCAM Murcia]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Udoka firma por el UCAM Murcia |url=http://www.ucamdeportes.com/ucamcb/noticia/3731 |website=ucamdeportes.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327112610/http://www.ucamdeportes.com/ucamcb/noticia/3731 |archive-date=March 27, 2020 |date=January 5, 2012}}</ref>

==Coaching career==

===San Antonio Spurs (2012–2019)===
On August 28, 2012, the [[San Antonio Spurs]] hired Udoka as an assistant coach under [[Gregg Popovich]].<ref>{{cite web |date=August 28, 2012 |title=Ime Udoka Joins Spurs Coaching Staff |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/120828_udoka |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140408214928/https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/120828_udoka |archive-date=April 8, 2014 |access-date=March 27, 2020 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Udoka won his first NBA championship when the Spurs defeated the [[Miami Heat]] in five games during the [[2014 NBA Finals]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 15, 2014 |title=Spurs shake early deficit to snuff out Heat and win 5th NBA title |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400559378 |access-date=June 20, 2014 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> Udoka was also the key for [[LaMarcus Aldridge]]'s decision to join the Spurs in 2015 as they were teammates on the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] during Aldridge's [[2006–07 NBA season|rookie season]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=LaMarcus Aldridge: Ime Udoka got the Spurs deal done |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2015/08/24/lamarcus-aldridge-san-antonio-spurs-ime-udoka |magazine=Sports Illustrated |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905091623/https://www.si.com/nba/2015/08/24/lamarcus-aldridge-san-antonio-spurs-ime-udoka |archive-date=September 5, 2015 |date=August 24, 2015}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2019–2020)===
On June 26, 2019, Udoka was hired as an assistant coach of the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web |date=June 26, 2019 |title=Udoka, Blair Added as Assistant Coaches |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/udoka-blair-added-assistant-coaches |access-date=June 26, 2019 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> His head coach on the 76ers at the time, [[Brett Brown]], also coached under Gregg Popovich for the Spurs, and both Udoka and Brown were on the same staff in the 2012–13 season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Brett Brown|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/coaches/brownbr99c.html|access-date=2021-08-31|website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2020–2021)===
On October 30, 2020, the [[Brooklyn Nets]] hired Udoka as an assistant coach.<ref>{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Announce Coaching Staff |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/10/30/brooklyn-nets-announce-coaching-staff |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 30, 2020 |date=October 30, 2020}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2021–2023)===

====2021–22 season====
[[File:Име Удока (2021).png|thumb|200px|Udoka in 2021]]
On June 23, 2021, it was reported that the [[Boston Celtics]] had hired Udoka as their head coach, replacing [[Brad Stevens]], who was promoted to President of Basketball Operations a few weeks prior.<ref>{{cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |date=June 23, 2021 |title=Boston Celtics finalizing choaching deal with Brooklyn Nets' Ime Udoka, sources say |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31694434 |access-date=June 30, 2021 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Kaskey-Blomain |first=Michael |date=June 23, 2021 |title=Boston Celtics to hire Ime Udoka: Brooklyn Nets Assistant to be named new coach, per report |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/boston-celtics-to-hire-ime-udoka-brooklyn-nets-assistant-to-be-named-new-coach-per-report/ |access-date=June 26, 2021 |website=cbssports.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Westerholm |first=Tom |date=June 23, 2021 |title=7 things to know about Ime Udoka, the new Celtics head coach |url=https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2021/06/23/ime-udoka-celtics-coach-things-to-know/ |access-date=June 25, 2021 |website=www.boston.com |language=en-US}}</ref> The hiring became official five days later.<ref>{{cite web |date=June 28, 2021 |title=Celtics Name Ime Udoka 18th Head Coach in Franchise History |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-name-ime-udoka-18th-head-coach-franchise-history |access-date=June 29, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=June 28, 2021 |title=Celtics hire Nets assistant Ime Udoka as next coach |url=https://www.nba.com/news/celtics-hire-ime-udoka-next-coach |access-date=June 29, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hightower |first=Kyle |date=June 28, 2021 |title=Celtics coach Ime Udoka ready to push Boston's stars |url=https://www.nba.com/news/celtics-coach-ime-udoka-wants-to-bring-the-dog-out-in-stars |access-date=July 1, 2021 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref> Udoka became the franchise's sixth African-American head coach, as well as the first head coach of African origin in NBA history.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2021-06-28|title=New Celtics head coach Ime Udoka's path from Nigeria to Boston|url=https://andscape.com/features/new-celtics-head-coach-ime-udoka-path-from-nigeria-to-boston/|access-date=2021-08-31|website=[[Andscape]]}}</ref> Stevens later stated that he hired Udoka as his own replacement as head coach since Udoka had "a great approachability".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sy |first=Bill |date=2021-10-29 |title=Brad Stevens on Ime Udoka, public criticism, and Marcus Smart |url=https://www.celticsblog.com/2021/10/29/22752674/brad-stevens-on-ime-udoka-public-criticism-and-marcus-smart-boston-celtics-jaylen-brown |access-date=October 31, 2021 |website=CelticsBlog |language=en}}</ref>

Although the Celtics began the [[2021–22 Boston Celtics season|2021–22 season]] with an 18–21 record, they began a turnaround in January and finished as the #2-seed in the Eastern Conference with a 51–31 record.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hartwell |first=Darren |date=March 24, 2022 |title=This stat puts Celtics' insane second-half turnaround in perspective |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/boston/celtics/celtics-crazy-second-half-turnaround-summed-great-stat |access-date=2022-05-26 |website=NBC Sports Boston}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=April 11, 2022 |title=An Appreciation For Celtics' Incredible Second-Half Turnaround |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/celtics-second-half-turnaround-appreciation-udoka-tatum-brown-smart-horford-stevens-nba/ |access-date=2022-05-26 |website=CBS Boston}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Quinn |first=Justin |date=2022-04-11 |title=Reacting to Celtics' remarkable turnaround since January: From 11-seed to 'best team in basketball' |url=https://celticswire.usatoday.com/2022/04/11/nba-boston-celtics-second-half-turnaround-reflection/ |access-date=2022-05-26 |website=Celtics Wire}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mannix |first=Chris |date=2022-06-08 |title=Inside the Celtics’ Dramatic Turnaround From Under .500 to NBA Finals |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2022/06/08/boston-celtics-nba-finals-jayson-tatum-ime-udoka-daily-cover |access-date=2025-08-18 |website=SI |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Manning |first=Bobby |date=2022-04-12 |title=Ime Udoka’s historic Celtics turnaround changed Boston’s outlook ===Houston Rockets (2023–present)===
====2023–24 season====
[[File:Ime Udoka Reeds press conference.png|thumb|Udoka in 2024]]On April 24, 2023, it was reported that the [[Houston Rockets]] hired Udoka as their head coach.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Quinn |first=Sam |date=2023-04-24 |title=Ime Udoka agrees to become head coach of the Houston Rockets, per report |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/ime-udoka-agrees-to-become-head-coach-of-the-houston-rockets-per-report/ |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}}</ref> The hiring became official the next day.<ref name=":1">{{cite web |title=Rockets Name Ime Udoka Head Coach |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-name-ime-udoka-head-coach |access-date=April 25, 2023 |website=NBA.com |date=April 25, 2023}}</ref>

Udoka was named Western Conference Coach of the Month in March 2024 after the Rockets won 13 of their 15 games that month.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rockets Ime Udoka Named Western Conference Coach of the Month |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-ime-udoka-named-western-conference-coach-of-the-month |access-date=April 3, 2024 |website=NBA.com |date=April 2, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Leger |first=Justin |title=Mazzulla, Udoka earn Coach of the Month honors for March |url=https://www.nbcsportsboston.com/nba/boston-celtics/joe-mazzulla-ime-udoka-nba-coach-of-the-month/600223/ |access-date=April 3, 2024 |website=NBC Sports Boston |date=April 2, 2024}}</ref> In his first season with the team, the Rockets finished with a 41–41 record and narrowly missed the playoffs.<ref>{{cite web |last=Davis |first=Coty M. |title=Rockets' Ime Udoka Finishes Seventh in NBA Coach of the Year Voting |url=https://www.si.com/nba/rockets/houston-rockets-ime-udoka-finishes-seventh-coach-of-year-voting |access-date=April 30, 2024 |website=Inside The Rockets |date=April 29, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ime Udoka on Rockets .500 Record to End 2023-24 Season: 'We Have Something to Build On' |url=https://athlonsports.com/nba/houston-rockets/inside-rockets/news/ime-udoka-houston-rockets-500-record-to-end-2023-24-season |access-date=April 15, 2024 |website=Athlon Sports |date=April 14, 2024}}</ref>

====2024–25 season====
Udoka was named Western Conference Coach of the Month in January 2025 after the Rockets won 11 of their 15 games that month.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rockets Ime Udoka Named Western Conference Coach of the Month for January |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-ime-udoka-named-western-conference-coach-of-the-month-for-january |access-date=February 9, 2025 |website=NBA.com |date=February 3, 2025}}</ref> They ultimately finished with a 52–30 record to clinch the [[Southwest Division (NBA)|Southwest Division]] for the first time in six years and finished as the #2-seed in the conference for the [[2025 NBA playoffs|2025 playoffs]], behind the No. 1 seed [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web |last=DuBose |first=Ben |title=By the numbers: Rockets finish regular season at 52-30, No. 2 in West |url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/rockets/2025/04/13/by-the-numbers-rockets-finish-regular-season-at-52-30-no-2-in-west/83071825007/ |access-date=July 7, 2025 |website=Rockets Wire |date=April 13, 2025}}</ref> However, the Rockets lost to the Warriors in seven games during the first round of the playoffs.<ref>{{cite web |title=Stephen Curry and Buddy Hield lead Warriors past Rockets 103-89 in Game 7 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401767914 |access-date=July 7, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |date=May 4, 2025}}</ref>

====2025–26 season====
On June 19, 2025, Udoka signed a multi-year contract extension with the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |title=Sources: Udoka joins tier of top-paid coaches |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45538712/sources-rockets-ime-udoka-agree-long-term-extension |access-date=July 7, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |date=June 19, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Rieken |first=Kristie |title=Reports: Ime Udoka, Rockets agree to contract extension |url=https://www.nba.com/news/ime-udoka-rockets-contract-extension |access-date=July 7, 2025 |website=NBA.com |date=June 19, 2025}}</ref> In the midst of a blockbuster trade where [[Kevin Durant]] was acquired by the Rockets, they finished once again with a 52–30 record, this time as the #5-seed in the conference for the [[2026 NBA playoffs|2026 playoffs]], where the [[2025–26 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]] were waiting for them. Although Durant remained healthy in the regular season, with his near-total absence in the playoffs, the Rockets lost to the Lakers in six games during the first round.

==National team career==
Udoka was a player on the [[Nigeria national basketball team|Nigerian national team]]. At the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]]s, he led Nigeria in scoring, assists, and steals.<ref name=":0" /> Udoka also played for Nigeria in the [[2005 FIBA Africa Championship|2005]] and [[AfroBasket 2011|2011]] [[AfroBasket|FIBA Africa Championships]], winning a bronze medal in both tournaments.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Who is Ime Udoka? Four things to know about Celtics' next head coach|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/ime-udoka-celtics-head-coach/10ebttxf6gvxm12mhtrzk3dg5j|access-date=2021-08-31|website=www.sportingnews.com|date=August 12, 2021 }}</ref>

Udoka has served as an assistant coach for [[United States men's national basketball team|USA Basketball]] under his Spurs head coach, Gregg Popovich. Udoka's coaching role on the [[2019 United States FIBA Basketball World Cup team|2019 FIBA World Cup team]] helped him build relationships with Celtics players [[Jayson Tatum]], [[Jaylen Brown]], and [[Marcus Smart]], who advocated for his hiring as the new Celtics head coach.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Helin|first=Kurt|date=2021-06-23|title=Report: Celtics to hire Ime Udoka as new head coach|url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2021/06/23/report-celtics-to-hire-ime-udoka-as-new-head-coach/|access-date=2021-08-31|website=NBC Sports}}</ref> Udoka also coached for Team USA under Popovich at the [[Basketball at the 2020 Summer Olympics|2020 Summer Olympics]] in Tokyo, along with Celtics assistant Will Hardy.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hartwell |first=Darren |date=July 10, 2021 |title=How Celtics fans can watch Jayson Tatum, Team USA play this week |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/boston/celtics/how-watch-jayson-tatum-ime-udoka-and-team-usa-basketball |access-date=2025-04-07 |website=NBC Sports Boston |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Udoka's father, Vitalis, was of Nigerian descent,<ref name="goviks" /> which qualified Udoka for Nigerian citizenship. His older sister, [[Mfon Udoka|Mfon]], played in the [[WNBA]]. Udoka's mother, Agnes, who died in late 2011, was an American from Illinois.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mazzeo |first1=Mike |title=Udoka dealing with tragedy |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/new-york/new-jersey-nets/post/_/id/2610 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327120002/https://www.espn.com/blog/new-york/new-jersey-nets/post/_/id/2610 |archive-date=March 27, 2020 |date=December 15, 2011}}</ref>

In February 2010, Udoka met actress [[Nia Long]] and they later began a relationship.<ref name="x433">{{cite web | last=Eidell | first=Lynsey | title=Nia Long and Ime Udoka's Relationship Timeline | website=People.com | date=2022-06-07 | url=https://people.com/sports/nia-long-ime-udoka-relationship-timeline/ | access-date=2025-01-25}}</ref> On November 7, 2011, Long gave birth to their first child, a son named Kez Sunday.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Finn |first1=Natalie |title=Nia Long gives birth to her second son |url=https://www.today.com/news/nia-long-gives-birth-her-second-son-wbna45237672 |website=today.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327121923/https://www.today.com/news/nia-long-gives-birth-her-second-son-wbna45237672 |archive-date=March 27, 2020 |date=November 10, 2011}}</ref> Udoka and Long got engaged in May 2015,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mackie |first1=Drew |title=Nia Long Is Engaged to Ime Udoka |url=https://people.com/celebrity/nia-long-engaged-to-ime-udoka/ |website=people.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170308135757/https://people.com/celebrity/nia-long-engaged-to-ime-udoka/ |archive-date=March 8, 2017 |date=May 26, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Nessif|first=Bruna|date=May 27, 2015|title=Nia Long Engaged to Longtime Boyfriend Ime Udoka—See the Ring!|work=[[E! News]]|url=https://www.eonline.com/news/660124/nia-long-engaged-to-longtime-boyfriend-ime-udoka|access-date=May 8, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Grant |first=Jasmine |date=July 24, 2020 |title=Exclusive: Nia Long Explains Why She's Not A Fan of Marriage |url=https://www.essence.com/love/nia-long-on-marriage/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200727230113/https://www.essence.com/love/nia-long-on-marriage/ |archive-date=July 27, 2020 |access-date=May 8, 2021 |work=[[Essence (magazine)|Essence]] |issn=0014-0880}}</ref> but they split in December 2022, a few months after Udoka's affair with a female Celtics staff member came to light.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Preezy |date=2022-12-07 |title=Nia Long And Ime Udoka Break Up After Celtics Cheating Scandal |url=https://www.vibe.com/news/entertainment/nia-long-ime-udoka-breakup-celtics-1234717225/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=VIBE.com}}</ref>
